summary.headline: Kross Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 225.4 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.9%; management guides 14-15% margins and FY27 growth near 22%.
summary.overview: Kross closed FY26 with revenue of INR 673.2 crore (+8.5%) and PAT of INR 55.2 crore (8.2% margin), after a slow H1 and a stronger H2 (H2 revenue 49.2% above H1). Q4 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 225.4 crore, EBITDA rose 25% to INR 33.6 crore and PAT rose 31% to INR 22.4 crore. Management says the Middle East conflict caused LPG shortages and commodity and consumable cost increases in Q4, with steel price hikes of INR 3-5/kg expected from April and a retrospective OEM pass-through lagging by about one quarter. The company has raised prices about 5% in trailer axles and suspensions and says it has fully deployed IPO proceeds.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA growth stated as 8.2% (transcript reads 87.9%, likely a transcription error)

financial_highlights.value: Trailer axles and suspension 43%; other components 57%

segments.name: Trailer axles and suspension
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes were over 10,500 trailer axles and over 3,500 suspension units, with air and mechanical suspension leading the pick-up. Q4 mix was about 60% suspension and 40% axles, and FY26 axle to suspension mix was about 70:30.

segments.name: Tipping Jacks (new)
segments.commentary: Launched and validated in Q4 FY26, with 75-80 kits sold in Q4 and 150-200 kits guided for Q1 FY27. Management targets 300 units by end-Q1 and 500 units each in Q2 and Q3, and says revenue will pick up at 300-400 kits a month.

segments.name: Tractor and Agri
segments.commentary: Tractor is about 9% of revenue, with a target of about 15% within two years. A third large tractor OEM is to start revenue from Q1 FY27, alongside diversification with existing two OEMs into forgings, shafts and castings.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were 4% of FY26 revenue. Management cites secured orders from European Tier-1 customers and aims to raise the share over two years; export of extruded axles will wait until the line runs above 5,000 beams a month.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue growth of about 22% (Q4 rate) to continue in FY27, subject to demand; 45 days into Q1, trends were described as robust.
Gross margin / EBITDA margin guided at 14-15% for coming quarters; Q1 FY27 may see one to two points of pressure as commodity pass-through is retrospective by about one quarter.
Seamless tube plant expected to be commissioned by end-FY27 (Q4 FY27); its revenue contribution starts in FY28, after in-house consumption.
OEMs are targeting high single-digit volume growth for FY27 across CV segments, per management.
Capex guided at about INR 100 crore for seamless tube and INR 20-25 crore for other business in FY27, plus maintenance capex. About INR 60 crore was spent on seamless tube in FY26.
capex_capacity: Extruded axle beam line commissioned; trials are complete and axle sales are expected from late May or June 2026. Management says the line is producing or targeting upward of 5,000 axle beams a month, versus earlier stated capacity of 5,000 axles a month expanding to 7,500 with the new plant.
Seamless tube facility: construction almost complete. Piercer to be dispatched from China by end-May 2026; rotary hearth furnace from Wesman is being installed.
High Pressure Mold Line to be operational by September 2026, doubling casting capacity. Another casting line planned for September-October 2026.
New robotic forging facility for rear axle shafts to be ready for supply by September 2026. Multiple high-tonnage forging presses already commissioned.
Forging and machining expansion described as mostly complete; furnace fuel switched away from sole LPG dependence.
demand_pricing: Management says M&HCV demand is strong: Tata Motors and Ashok Leyland reported strong Q4 volume growth that continued in April 2026. Production runs above 10,000-12,000 trucks a month across the two largest CV OEMs, below the Feb-Mar peak of 14,000-15,000.
Price hike of about 5% taken in trailer axles and suspension, which the company says is in line with competitor moves of about 4%. Management says it cannot price above the #1 player.

Steel price increase of INR 3-5/kg being negotiated with OEMs from April 2026. Conversion cost increase requested for tooling, oils and gas. OEM pass-through is retrospective but delayed by about one quarter; axle and suspension business has no retrospective recovery.
Steel mills are holding about 50-60% of ordered stock, so supply is tight but available. LPG shortage led to furnace fuel changes.
Management says rail freight corridor will affect only a small portion of trailer demand, mainly rigid-body vehicles.
Demand from fabricators for extruded axles is strong, but the company cannot meet it yet due to ramp-up constraints.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the tractor target of about 15% of revenue, given single-digit tractor industry growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites new customer addition (third large tractor OEM starting Q1) and new products (forgings, shafts, castings) with the two existing OEMs, with the target over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 22% Q4 growth sustainable, and what are volume trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is planning for that pace if the last six months' tonnage and demand trends hold. Q1 FY27 is seen as better than Q1 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected commodity and margin impact in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel hike of INR 3-5/kg is effective April but retrospective recovery is delayed about one quarter, so Q1 margin pressure is expected. Management guides 14-15% margin for later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the seamless tube capex and when does revenue start?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 60 crore was spent in FY26, with about INR 100 crore planned for FY27. Plant commissioning is expected around Q4 FY27 and revenue from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the rail freight corridor affect trailer demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact will be limited to a small portion of trailer demand and would mainly affect rigid-body vehicles.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 margin pressure from steel and consumable cost increases before OEM settlement, with the retrospective recovery delayed about one quarter.
Fuel-price and LPG shortage effects on CV operator demand and on the company's furnace-based heat treatment.
Ramp-up of the extruded axle line to the 5,000+ beams/month level, and the Tipping Jacks targets of 300/500 units per quarter.
Seamless tube commissioning slippage beyond Q4 FY27; seamless revenue is not expected until FY28.
Tractor target of about 15% revenue within two years depends on the third OEM's ramp-up and new product wins.
Q2 monsoon seasonality in CV demand. Management noted weaker Q2 seasonality.
Note the transcript contains an apparent error in the FY26 EBITDA growth figure ('87.9%'), and the Q4 PAT margin ('69 bps') and the Q4 EBITDA margin of 14.9% need checking against filings.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and capacity additions, with specific timelines for the new lines. Cautious on Q1 FY27 margins, which are exposed to commodity pass-through lags, and on sustaining 22% growth, which management says is conditional on demand. Some answers were vague on quantification, for example the FY27 revenue target and the export timeline.
key_quotes: Although the demand has been good, it has overall been a challenging Q4 with the Middle East conflict resulting in the shortage of LPG and a substantial increase in commodity prices and consumables.
At the moment, we are struggling to meet the demand which is being given to us, struggling to ramp up to meet our peak capacity. But, this is a temporary hiccup.
But between 14% to 15% margin is what we are looking at for the further quarters as well.
So, it is not going to be in this financial year that the seamless tube will contribute towards revenue growth.

adds.what: Extruded axle beam line (5,000 beams/month; expanding to 7,500 with new plant)
Seamless tube plant (revenue contribution from FY28)
High pressure mold line doubling casting capacity
Robotic forging facility for rear axle shafts

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 22% (subject to demand), backed partly by the extruded axle line in trials, a Tipping Jacks launch (150-200 kits guided for Q1), a third tractor OEM from Q1 FY27 and strong demand, but with no numbers on the total order book and the seamless tube plant contributing only from FY28.
